producer_report.summary: The States, Counters, Transitions and Why sections now each open with a short plain-words lead-in that cites claims. Every state, counter and transition has a one-line summary. On a transition card the summary comes before the trigger and guard fields. The cards now say who decides: "the agent, by judgment" or "code, a fixed script check". State kinds read as plain labels, for example "where work starts" instead of "initial". The glossary gains "code" and "session start". The lead-ins are in intro.json under `lead_ins` and the summaries are in model.json. The renderer rejects a missing, unknown-claim or uncited lead-in, and a card with no summary. I did not run `cargo run -p xtask -- site` itself; a test renders the real study from the same data and asserts the lead-ins and 8 summaries. Rust checks passed (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --locked -p xtask`). I did not run the full workspace `cargo test --locked`.

checks_run.note: 15 unit tests and 9 policy tests, including 3 new site tests and the updated real-study test
only the xtask package was run

open_issues: Summaries carry no claim ids of their own. They are covered by the claims of the state, counter or transition they sit in, so a summary sentence is not checked against its claims individually. This follows the brief's 'no new claims' limit, and the design doc and changelog say so.
Transition t5 and t7 still show 'Guard: none (checked by the agent)', which is the existing model data and reads oddly.
I did not check the deployed page. The live GitHub Pages site still needs a workflow run after merge.
mistakes: My first CHANGELOG edit failed because the anchor matched six places. I retried with the '## [Unreleased]' heading included.
learnings: Existing intro tests wrote whole intro.json files inline. Once lead-ins became required, they would have errored for the wrong reason, so I rebuilt them from shared fixture constants.
Rationale cards (ra1 to ra4) have no summary field, and rationales.json is not in the deliverables. The Why lead-in covers them, and the card text is already a plain sentence.
The boundary-word policy test (`athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where`) scans tracked files, and it passes.
desires: A way to check each plain-language summary against the quotes in its claims, to catch drift.
